questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Preamble of the Indian Constitution:
1. The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added by the 42nd Amendment Act.
2. In the Berubari Union case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
3. In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In Berubari (1960) the Court held the Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution; Kesavananda (1973) reversed this. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Socialist, Secular and Integrity.
questions.h: Berubari said no, Kesavananda said yes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Protection under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
2. Article 19 freedoms are suspended automatically when Emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression.
3. Article 14 is available to foreigners as well as citizens.
4. Article 19 freedoms are available to foreigners residing in India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment bars suspension of Articles 20 and 21 (Art 359); Art 358 suspends Art 19 automatically for war/external aggression; Art 14 applies to 'any person'. Art 19 is for citizens only, so statement 4 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the battles?
questions.e: Plassey (1757) gave the British Bengal; Wandiwash (1760) ended French power in the Carnatic; Buxar (1764) confirmed British supremacy over Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II.
questions.s: Spectrum, Ch 'Expansion and Consolidation of British Power'

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Harappan Civilisation is NOT correct?
o: Lothal is associated with a dockyard
Harappan people used iron tools extensively for agriculture and construction
Dholavira has an elaborate system of water reservoirs
The Great Bath is located at Mohenjodaro
questions.e: The Harappans were a Bronze Age (chalcolithic) people; iron came into wide use in India only later, around 1000 BCE. Lothal's dockyard, Dholavira's reservoirs and Mohenjodaro's Great Bath are all correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History I, Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Earth is at perihelion around 3 January.
2. The Earth is at aphelion around 4 July.
3. The change of seasons is caused primarily by the varying distance of the Earth from the Sun.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis (66.5 degrees to the orbital plane) and parallelism of the axis, not distance; India is hottest in summer when the Earth is farthest from the Sun.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 8

questions.q:
Statement-I: When the RBI sells government securities in the open market, liquidity in the banking system declines.
Statement-II: Buyers of the securities pay for them from their bank balances, which reduces the reserves of commercial banks.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Open market sales drain money: payments for securities reduce bank reserves with the RBI, tightening liquidity. Statement-II is the mechanism behind Statement-I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings.
2. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
3. Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts.
4. Effective revenue deficit is revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are the standard definitions used in the Union Budget documents and the FRBM framework.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Minamata Convention : Mercury
2. Rotterdam Convention : Prior informed consent for trade in hazardous chemicals and pesticides
3. Stockholm Convention : Persistent organic pollutants
4. Basel Convention : Ozone-depleting substances
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Basel Convention regulates the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes; ozone-depleting substances are covered by the Montreal Protocol.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A geostationary satellite orbits at about 36,000 km above the equator.
2. A geostationary satellite has an orbital period equal to the Earth's rotation period.
3. Geostationary satellites provide good coverage of the polar regions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Geostationary satellites sit above the equator (about 35,786 km) with a 24-hour period, so they appear fixed. From the equatorial plane the poles are seen at a grazing angle, so polar coverage is poor; polar orbiting satellites serve those regions.
questions.s: NCERT / ISRO basics; Standard S&T text

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution can the Governor promulgate ordinances when the State Legislature is not in session?
questions.e: Article 213 gives the Governor ordinance-making power (parallel to Article 123 for the President). Article 200 relates to assent to Bills, Article 161 to pardoning power and Article 356 to President's Rule.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Supreme Court judge can be removed only by the President on an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority.
2. A retired High Court judge cannot plead or act before any court in India.
3. The salaries of Supreme Court judges are charged to the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 124(4) prescribes removal by address of both Houses; Article 112 charges judges' salaries to the Consolidated Fund. Article 220 bars a retired High Court judge only from practising in the High Court where he served; he may practise in the Supreme Court and other High Courts.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: Ashoka's inscriptions are found in different scripts in different parts of his empire.
Statement-II: In the north-west, Ashokan edicts were written in Kharosthi, Aramaic and Greek, while Brahmi was used in most of the rest of the empire.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Brahmi was used in the core and eastern/southern areas, while the north-west edicts (Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra, Kandahar) used Kharosthi, Aramaic or Greek to suit local readers. Statement-II explains the variety noted in Statement-I.
questions.s: Romila Thapar / NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History I, Ch 2

questions.q: Which one of the following rivers is a tributary of the Yamuna?
questions.e: Betwa, Ken, Chambal and Sindh join the Yamuna from the south. Son joins the Ganga from the south, while Gandak and Kosi join the Ganga from the north (Himalayas).
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Wholesale Price Index does not include services.
2. The Consumer Price Index (Combined) is released by the National Statistics Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
3. The Wholesale Price Index is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
4. The Consumer Price Index is compiled by the Reserve Bank of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: WPI covers goods only and is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry); CPI is compiled and released by the NSO (MoSPI), not the RBI, which only uses it for its inflation-targeting framework.

questions.q: Which one of the following global biodiversity hotspots does NOT include any part of the Indian territory?
questions.e: India's hotspots are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats (with Sri Lanka) and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands). Wallacea lies in Indonesia between the Asian and Australian shelves.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sequences.
2. DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.
3. Taq polymerase used in PCR is obtained from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus.
4. Plasmids are circular DNA found only within the chromosomes of eukaryotic cells.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Taq polymerase withstands the high temperatures of PCR cycles because it comes from a heat-loving bacterium. Plasmids are extra-chromosomal circular DNA found chiefly in bacteria, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Ch 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Panchayati Raj:
1. The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects for Panchayats.
2. The State Finance Commission is constituted every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats.
3. The State Election Commissioner for Panchayat elections is appointed by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 243I and 243K: the Governor constitutes the Finance Commission every five years and appoints the State Election Commissioner (not the President). The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Young Bengal Movement : Ram Mohan Roy
questions.e: Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) to challenge Brahmanical dominance. The Prarthana Samaj was led by Atmaram Pandurang, the Arya Samaj by Dayananda Saraswati, and Young Bengal by Henry Derozio.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Parliament can create a new All-India Service by law.
Statement-II: Under Article 312, the Rajya Sabha must first pass a resolution supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting declaring that it is necessary in the national interest.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 312 gives the Rajya Sabha, representing the States, a special role: it must first authorise the creation of an All-India Service by such a resolution, after which Parliament legislates. Statement-II explains how the power in Statement-I operates.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Services under the Union and the States'

questions.q: Which one of the following is responsible for winter rainfall in north-western India that benefits the rabi wheat crop?
questions.e: Western disturbances are extra-tropical cyclonic systems from the Mediterranean region, steered by the westerly jet stream into north-west India in winter. The north-east monsoon rains Tamil Nadu coast; Kalbaisakhi is a pre-monsoon summer thunderstorm.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: The Third Buddhist Council, held at Pataliputra during the reign of Ashoka, was presided over by whom?
questions.e: The Third Council (c. 250 BCE) under Ashoka was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa and is linked to the compilation of the Abhidhamma Pitaka. Mahakassapa presided over the First Council, and Vasumitra over the Fourth under Kanishka.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History I, Ch 4; Nitin Singhania, Ch 'Religion'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:
1. He can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.
2. He is not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or of any State after ceasing to hold his office.
3. His reports relating to the accounts of a State are submitted to the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 148 provides for removal like a Supreme Court judge and bars further government office, protecting independence. Under Article 151, State audit reports go to the Governor, who lays them before the State Legislature.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Comptroller and Auditor General of India'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Peru (Humboldt) Current is a warm current.
2. The Agulhas Current is a warm current flowing along the east coast of southern Africa.
3. The Falkland Current is a cold current.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Peru Current carries cold water northward along South America's west coast (it is linked to upwelling and rich fisheries; El Nino reverses this with warm water). Agulhas is warm, Falkland is cold.
questions.s: Certificate Physical and Human Geography, Ch 'Ocean Currents'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Minimum Support Price (MSP):
1. MSPs are recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.
2. The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices is a constitutional body.
3. MSPs are approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CACP is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, not a constitutional body. It recommends MSPs; the CCEA takes the final decision.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol aims at phasing down the production and consumption of hydrofluorocarbons.
Statement-II: Hydrofluorocarbons are major ozone-depleting substances.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: HFCs were introduced to replace ozone-depleting CFCs and HCFCs; they do not contain chlorine and so do not deplete ozone, but they are potent greenhouse gases. Kigali targets them for their climate warming effect.

questions.q: Which one of the following Acts designated the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India?
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1833 centralised legislative and administrative power in the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck became the first) and ended the Company's commercial functions. The 1773 Act created the post of Governor-General of Bengal.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Beriberi : Deficiency of thiamine (Vitamin B1)
2. Scurvy : Deficiency of Vitamin K
3. Rickets : Deficiency of Vitamin A
4. Pellagra : Deficiency of niacin (Vitamin B3)
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C deficiency (Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting) and rickets by Vitamin D deficiency (Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness).
questions.s: Standard General Science text, vitamins and deficiency diseases

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India:
1. It conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.
3. It conducts elections to the offices of the President and the Vice-President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 324 vests the ECI with superintendence of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President. Local body elections are conducted by State Election Commissions (Articles 243K and 243ZA).

questions.q: Which one of the following is recorded in the current account of India's Balance of Payments?
o: External commercial borrowings by Indian firms
Remittances sent home by Indians working abroad
Deposits of Non-Resident Indians in Indian banks
questions.e: Remittances are secondary income transfers and therefore sit in the current account. FDI, ECBs and NRI deposits are capital/financial account flows that create liabilities or assets.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972:
1. The National Tiger Conservation Authority is a statutory body under the Act.
2. Hunting of animals listed in Schedule I is prohibited without any exception whatsoever.
3. The National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2006 amendment gave statutory status to the NTCA; the NBWL is chaired by the Prime Minister. Section 11 permits hunting of even Schedule I animals in narrow cases, such as an animal dangerous to human life or disabled/diseased beyond recovery, with the Chief Wildlife Warden's permission.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Ch 'Wildlife Protection Act'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balban introduced the practices of Sijda and Paibos in his court.
2. Firuz Shah Tughlaq introduced token currency made of copper and brass.
3. Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and copper jital as standard coins.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The token currency experiment was by Muhammad bin Tughlaq (copper/brass tokens), not Firuz Shah; it failed because forgery was easy. Balban's court ceremonies asserted royal dignity, and Iltutmish standardised the tanka and jital.
questions.s: Satish Chandra, Medieval India; NCERT Class XI Themes in Indian History

questions.q: Arrange the following battles of the Mughal and Sur period in correct chronological order.
o: Chausa - Khanwa - Kannauj - Second Battle of Panipat
Khanwa - Kannauj - Chausa - Second Battle of Panipat
Khanwa - Chausa - Kannauj - Second Battle of Panipat
Chausa - Kannauj - Khanwa - Second Battle of Panipat
questions.e: Babur defeated Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527); Sher Shah beat Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540), driving him out; Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan defeated Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).
questions.s: Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.q: Which one of the following temples is correctly matched with the dynasty that built it?
questions.e: Khajuraho's temples were built by the Chandelas. The Shore temple is Pallava, the Kailasa temple at Ellora was commissioned by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, and the Dilwara Jain temples belong to the Solanki (Chaulukya) period.

questions.q: Which one of the following mountain passes is correctly matched with the route it serves?
questions.e: Bhor Ghat carries the Mumbai-Pune route and Thal Ghat the Mumbai-Nashik route. The Palghat Gap links Kerala (Palakkad) with Tamil Nadu (Coimbatore), and Nathu La connects Sikkim with Tibet.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Ch 'Physiography'; NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Cash Reserve Ratio, scheduled banks keep a percentage of their net demand and time liabilities as cash with the RBI.
2. The Statutory Liquidity Ratio can be maintained in cash, gold or approved securities.
3. The RBI pays interest to banks on the balances kept under the Cash Reserve Ratio.
4. The Statutory Liquidity Ratio is maintained with the RBI.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CRR balances are held with the RBI and earn no interest, while SLR is maintained by banks themselves in the form of liquid assets such as cash, gold and government securities.

questions.q: Which one of the following Five Year Plans in India placed emphasis on rapid industrialisation, especially heavy industries, based on the Mahalanobis model?
questions.e: The First Plan (1951-56) was agriculture-focused and based on the Harrod-Domar model. The Second Plan (1956-61), drafted under P. C. Mahalanobis, prioritised capital goods and heavy industry, supported by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Biochemical Oxygen Demand measures the oxygen needed by microorganisms to decompose organic matter in water.
2. A high Biochemical Oxygen Demand indicates a lower level of organic pollution.
3. Eutrophication caused by nutrient enrichment can reduce dissolved oxygen in a water body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: High BOD means a lot of biodegradable organic matter, so more oxygen is consumed and the water is more polluted. Excess nutrients cause algal blooms whose decay depletes dissolved oxygen.

questions.q: Which one of the following describes 'green hydrogen'?
o: Hydrogen produced by electrolysis of water using renewable electricity
Hydrogen produced from natural gas with carbon capture and storage
Hydrogen produced from natural gas without carbon capture
questions.e: Green hydrogen has no carbon emissions at the production stage because the electricity for electrolysis is renewable. Hydrogen from natural gas with carbon capture is called blue, without capture grey, and from coal brown or black.
questions.s: Standard S&T text; MNRE National Green Hydrogen Mission documents

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Astra is a surface-to-air missile.
2. BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia.
3. Akash is a surface-to-air missile system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Astra is an indigenous beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, not a surface-to-air missile. BrahMos came from the India-Russia joint venture of DRDO and NPO Mashinostroyeniya, and Akash is a medium-range surface-to-air system.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding intellectual property in India:
1. A patent is granted for a term of 20 years from the date of filing the application.
2. Copyright in a literary work lasts for the lifetime of the author plus 70 years.
3. Registration of a Geographical Indication is valid for 10 years and can be renewed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under the Copyright Act, 1957 the term is the author's lifetime plus 60 years, not 70. The Patents Act, 1970 gives a 20-year term from filing, and the GI Act, 1999 gives 10-year renewable registration.
questions.s: Standard S&T text; Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (IPR)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Duties:
1. They are enforceable through writs issued by the courts.
2. They were incorporated on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
3. The duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child between six and fourteen years was added by the 86th Amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation. They are non-justiciable; the 11th duty came with the 86th Amendment (2002).

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles is correctly matched with the State to which it gives special provisions?
questions.e: Article 371J (98th Amendment, 2012) concerns the Hyderabad-Karnataka region. Article 371B relates to Assam, 371C to Manipur, 371F to Sikkim and 371G to Mizoram (371H is Arunachal Pradesh).
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Special Provisions for Some States'

questions.q:
Statement-I: Parliament can alter the boundaries or name of a State by an ordinary law under Article 3.
Statement-II: A law made under Article 3 must be passed by a special majority as it is treated as an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 4 specifically says laws under Articles 2 and 3 are not deemed amendments under Article 368, so a simple majority suffices (the President must refer the Bill to the affected State Legislature for its views, which are not binding).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the anti-defection law:
1. The Tenth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985.
2. The question of disqualification of a member of Parliament on grounds of defection is decided by the President in all cases.
3. The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 removed the exemption for a split in a legislature party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Presiding Officer of the House (Speaker or Chairman) decides disqualification, though the decision is subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan). The 91st Amendment deleted the one-third 'split' protection, leaving only merger (two-thirds).

questions.q: Which one of the following policies is correctly matched with the Governor-General associated with it?
o: Permanent Settlement of Bengal : Lord Wellesley
questions.e: Dalhousie annexed states like Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur by lapse. Subsidiary Alliance is Wellesley's, Permanent Settlement (1793) Cornwallis's, and the Vernacular Press Act (1878) was passed under Lytton; Ripon repealed it.
questions.s: Spectrum, Ch 'Expansion and Consolidation of British Power'
questions.h: Cornwallis land, Wellesley alliances, Dalhousie lapse

questions.q:
As per Census 2011, consider the following statements:
1. The sex ratio of India was 943 females per 1000 males.
2. Uttar Pradesh had the highest population density among all States.
3. Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest population density among all States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bihar, not Uttar Pradesh, was the most densely populated State (about 1,106 persons per sq km), while Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest density (about 17). The national sex ratio was 943.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act:
1. It guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
2. At least one-third of the beneficiaries are to be women.
3. The entire cost of the scheme is borne by the State Governments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act (2005) is a demand-driven legal guarantee. The Centre bears the full cost of unskilled wages and most of the material cost, so the claim that States bear the entire cost is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Ch 'Poverty, Unemployment and Rural Development'

questions.q:
Statement-I: Coral bleaching occurs when sea temperatures rise abnormally above the normal summer maximum.
Statement-II: Under thermal stress, corals expel the symbiotic zooxanthellae living in their tissues and turn white.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Zooxanthellae give corals their colour and food through photosynthesis. When heat stress makes them harmful, the polyps expel them, causing white (bleached) corals that may starve and die; Statement-II is the mechanism for Statement-I.

questions.q: Which one of the following Acts does NOT fall within the original jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal as listed in Schedule I of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
questions.e: Schedule I lists the Water Act, Water Cess Act, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Air Act, Environment (Protection) Act 1986, Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 and Biological Diversity Act. The Wildlife Act and the Indian Forest Act 1927 are not included.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a characteristic of the black cotton (regur) soil of the Deccan?
o: It becomes sticky when wet and develops deep cracks when dry
It is rich in nitrogen and humus
It is formed by the weathering of granite and gneiss
It is formed by intense leaching of silica and bases under heavy rainfall
questions.e: Regur soil forms from Deccan Trap basalt and has high clay content that retains moisture; it is rich in lime, iron and magnesium but poor in nitrogen and humus. Red soils come from granite/gneiss, laterites from leaching.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 6
